why: A census proves it counted; only a failed case proves the counter can fail. The A2A directory census had no negative control, so nothing in it could be read as evidence that the counter can reject.
rule: Where the estate's A2A agent is listed, and where it is not. Every row is a probe of the DIRECTORY, never of our own filesystem. This file mirrors mcp-directories.json deliberately: that file was wrong six times in one day, and every one of those errors came from answering 'do we hold a note saying we are listed' instead of asking the directory. UNKNOWN is a permitted state and is not NOT_LISTED.
rule_as_implemented: a probed row counts as a REAL directory iff state != 'NOT_A_DIRECTORY' and surface != 'ours'. UNKNOWN is a permitted state and is not NOT_LISTED.
rule_source: the census's own principle and surface_note; no new taxonomy is introduced here.

grader_can_fail.injected_defect: the `surface == 'ours'` exclusion is removed, so a row answered from our own filesystem would be counted as evidence about a third party

abort_rule: if any control fails, or the published census's own totals do not reproduce under this rule, the control run is ABORTED and the census is not re-published. A control that cannot fail is not a control.
what_this_does_not_establish: It does not re-run the census. The A2A directory census has no generator in this repository, so this control exercises the census's OWN published rule against its OWN published data.
It does not re-probe any directory. The states are as published on 2026-09-30.
It does not prove the probe of each directory was correct; it proves the COUNTING over the probes can reject a malformed row.
